newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar firmer in late Tokyo, holds above 118 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firmer in late Tokyo, holds above 118 yen.

text.p: 0656 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar was holding firmer against the yen in late Friday trade, with recent weakness in Japanese financial markets and the Asian currency crisis supporting the dollar's underlying bullishness, dealers said.
Mark buying against the yen in cross trade on speculation that the interest rate gap between Japan and Germany would widen also helped the dollar against the yen, dealers said.
Traders said a heavy volume of dollar purchases by interbank traders emerged in connection with buying of option positions by overseas operators.

Overseas operators bought dollar call options with strikes around 118.10 yen and a life of less than one week. Dollar firmness in afternoon trade forced traders who wrote the options to buy dollars to hedge their positions, accelerating the U.S. currency's rise to 118.44 yen before it retraced.
"We don't know what purpose they bought the calls for, but they certainly helped the dollar rise decisively above 118 yen," said a dealer at a U.S. bank in Tokyo.

"The yen is not a good currency to buy," said a dealer at a European bank in Tokyo. "It even failed to become a safe-haven currency amid the Asian currency turmoil, because of poor financial conditions and the fragile economy in Japan".
Traders began to think that given the magnitude of economic ties between Japan and other Asian nations, the worsening crisis in Asia would favour selling yen against the dollar.

"Given Japan's strong economic links with Asian nations, a worsening of the (Asia currency) situation would harm Japan and is likely to spur yen selling," said Hokuto Nakano, manager of Industrial Bank of Japan's international treasury department.
"Money fleeing Asian nations is mainly going to the United States, where the performance of the economy and the financial markets are far better than in Japan," he added.
The greenback strengthened in mid-morning trade as the key 182nd 10-year bond Japanese government bond (JGB) yield fell to an all-time record low of 2.065 percent.
Rumours that some Japanese construction companise were in financial trouble pushed the yen bond yield lower and depressed the Tokyo stock market. This in turn helped lift the dollar.
"It is possible that the dollar will re-test psychological resistance at 120 yen next week," said one dealer.
Dealers said exporters are unlikely to rush to sell dollars actively on Monday when they return from a summer holiday, due to the dollar's recovery to the level seen a week ago.

The focus will be on Japan's customs-cleared trade data for July, which will be released early on Monday. A Reuters poll of economists produced an average forecast of an 83 percent rise in the trade surplus from a year ago. Forecasts for the increase ranged from 60 percent to 114 percent, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
The dollar ended at 117.78/88 yen and 1.8390/00 marks in New York on Thursday.---Tatsuo Ito 81-3-3432-1396
